bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Cabinet Approves New Proposals Including New Universities - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Cabinet Approves New Proposals Including New Universities 26 Sep 2026 3 min read Why in News? The Bihar Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary , approved 24 proposals on 23 September 2026 , including the establishment of Maa Sita Women’s University in Patna and Ramdhari Singh Dinkar University in Begusarai . Key Points: Ramdhari Singh Dinkar University: The Cabinet approved the establishment of Ramdhari Singh Dinkar University in Begusarai . The university is proposed under the Bihar Special University Act, 2026 . Its jurisdiction will cover constituent and affiliated colleges in Begusarai and Khagaria , except institutions under Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University . Maa Sita Women’s University: The Cabinet also approved the establishment of Maa Sita Women’s University in Patna . It will have jurisdiction over constituent and affiliated women’s colleges in Patna , except those affiliated with Patna University . Livestock Farmers: The Cabinet approved the Mukhyamantri Go-Dhan Vikas Rin Yojana for livestock farmers. The scheme provides 100% subsidy on the interest component of eligible bank loans. Dairy Development: Eight dairy projects were approved for the Kosi region . The projects include the establishment of 500 new milk cooperative societies and expansion of dairy infrastructure. An estimated ₹126.07 crore has been approved for these projects. New Sugar Mill: Approval was given for establishing a new sugar mill at Warisaliganj in Nawada district . It is expected to support sugarcane farmers in Nawada, Nalanda, Sheikhpura and Jamui . Police Modernisation: The Cabinet approved ₹24.50 crore for procurement of 50 drones under the centrally sponsored police modernisation scheme. The drones will support activities such as crowd management, riverine operations, anti-Naxal operations and disaster management . Healthcare Digitisation: The Cabinet approved implementation of e-SushrutNX , developed by C-DAC , in 12 medical institutions . The system will digitise hospital processes beginning with patient registration and other treatment-related procedures. Fisheries Development: The Cabinet also approved ₹195.28 crore for transforming the Siwan Wetlands Cluster into an integrated aquaculture and export-oriented value chain under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) . national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 191 EAM Jaishankar calls for text based negotiations to ensure meaningful UN reforms
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar has said, frustration is growing within the international community over the lack of progress on reforming the United Nations. Dr Jaishankar was speaking at a ministerial session titled ‘Ruptures & Ramparts: Building Bridges for a Changing World’ on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York. The External Affairs Minister said there is a growing feeling that the UN must change and better reflect the realities of the world today. He said countries opposing UN reforms cannot continue to use the organisation without supporting efforts to strengthen it. Dr Jaishankar also rejected the idea that UN reform can be achieved through unanimity. Drawing a parallel with democratic decision-making, he said countries should be free to put forward their views, after which decisions should be taken through voting. He said this is essential for moving the reform process forward. He stressed that meaningful reform requires a concrete text that can be negotiated. The External Affairs Minister also said there is greater willingness among countries of the Global South to work together on the issue. He said, countries are increasingly willing to engage with one another and work together, which is a positive development as it helps break old dependencies and contributes to a more democratic and balanced world. His remarks come as UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has called for reform of the Security Council, saying it must better reflect today’s world and have greater legitimacy to address current geopolitical challenges. India has long advocated reform of the Security Council, including expansion of both its permanent and non-permanent membership. New Delhi has argued that the 15-member Council, created in 1945, does not adequately reflect contemporary geopolitical realities.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | Sports 55 Asian Games: India’s overall medal tally reaches 23, with 2 Gold, 9 Silver, 12 Bronze
national_raw_news.content: In the Asian Games, India’s overall medal tally has reached 23, with 2 Gold, 9 Silver and 12 Bronze in Japan. Indian duo Kamaljeet and Suruchi Singh won gold in the mixed team 10m air pistol event in Nagoya, Japan, today. The pair shot 484.6 in the final to finish 6.6 points ahead of South Korea’s Suhyeon Hong and Gaeun Choo, who took silver with 478. Indian long-distance runner Gulveer Singh won the silver medal in the men’s 10,000m race at the Asian Games. Indian athlete Baranica Elangovan won the bronze medal in the women’s pole vault at the Asian Games. Another Indian athlete, Manpreet Kaur, won the bronze medal in the women’s shot put. In Table Tennis, Indian Mixed Doubles pair of Diya Chitale and Manush Shah settled for a bronze medal after losing to World Champions and Chinese combination Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha 0-3. India’s men’s and women’s kabaddi teams have also entered the finals at the Asian Games after registering comprehensive victories in their respective semifinal matches. Indian squash players have assured themselves of three medals at the Asian Games, with Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar reaching the mixed doubles semifinals, while Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh entered the last four in singles.

national_raw_news.title: Manipur CM Announces Financial Assistance Scheme for Women Street Vendors 13 mins ago 3
national_raw_news.content: Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh today attended the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, 2026 in Manipur’s Bishnupur District. Addressing the gathering, the Chief Minister announced that a special financial assistance scheme for women street vendors of the State will be introduced before Ningol Chakouba, 2026 to help meet their families’ daily needs. He said those who are yet to register may do so through their respective MLAs. He said the month-long Seva Sankalp Abhiyan is being observed across the country to acknowledge 25 years of public service by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and to carry forward the spirit of public service and good governance. The Chief Minister said the 2023 crisis had a drastic impact on the State’s economy, incurring huge loss in GST revenue. He noted that frequent bandhs and blockades cause a loss of around Rs 25 to Rs 30 crore per day in tax revenue, and appealed that differences be settled through dialogue rather than agitations that affect normal life. Recalling his visit to Jiribam district, he said the trust deficit among different communities after the crisis has been substantially bridged and communities are now living in peace and harmony. Expressing anguish over the tragic incident at Tronglaobi that claimed the lives of two innocent siblings just after his Jiribam visit, he said certain vested interests continue to work against the government’s efforts to restore lasting peace. He informed that public transport services along NH-2 connecting Imphal with Guwahati via Dimapur have resumed and people are actively availing it. He encouraged people to visit the hills. The Chief Minister said the crisis has severely hit families dependent on daily wages. Following discussions in the recently concluded 8th Session of the 12th Manipur Legislative Assembly, the government has decided to extend financial assistance of Rs 10,000 each to around 3,00,050 families, for which budgetary provision has been earmarked. He appealed to all sections to keep aside differences and work together for unity and integrity of Manipur. During the programme, the Chief Minister distributed benefits under various government schemes to eligible beneficiaries of Bishnupur district and visited over 25 service counters and stalls showcasing schemes and services. Earlier in the day at Sanjenthong, Imphal East, the CM attended a function organised by the Department of Veterinary & Animal Husbandry for distribution of pregnant heifers to SC farmers under the NEC-funded project “Dairy Farming – A Way of Life for SC Farmers of Manipur”. In the first phase, 31 high-yielding pregnant heifers were distributed to 31 beneficiaries – 8 each from Thoubal, Kakching, Imphal West and 7 from Imphal East, selected through lottery. The programme was held in hybrid mode with 8 beneficiaries at Sanjenthong and 23 at Cattle Farm, Tangkham via live streaming. The CM encouraged scientific cattle rearing to boost milk production and household income. The project covers 612 beneficiaries across four districts and aims to increase milk production, promote socio-economic upliftment and generate employment. The Director (Vety & AH) urged beneficiaries to enrol the animals under the Livestock Insurance Scheme for which premium has been deposited with NICL, Imphal.

national_raw_news.title: UP Government Releases ₹403 Crore for Development of 4,030 Ambedkar Statue Sites 43 mins ago 20
national_raw_news.content: Uttar Pradesh government has released 403 crore rupees for development of 4,030 Ambedkar Statue Sites in the state. In the first phase of the Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Statue Site Development scheme, 10 statue sites in each of the 403 Assembly Constituencies, a total of 4,030 sites, will be developed. The scheme aims to provide a safe, protected, and dignified environment for statues of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and other great personalities installed in public places. On September 22, 2026, the Directorate allocated Rs 403 crore to District Magistrates for development of 4,030 statue sites. This translates into an average allocation of approximately Rs 10 lakh per statue site. Under the scheme, works such as installing railing-equipped steel staircases, constructing roofs over statues, building boundary walls, finishing work, and greenery and lighting arrangements will be undertaken. The scheme will also develop a clean, organized, and dignified environment around the sites. In addition, an information board measuring 3×2.5 feet displaying the name of the statue and a brief history will be installed at each site, subject to approval by the District Magistrate. The government has also laid down a timeline for speedy implementation of the scheme. Separate deadlines have been fixed for receiving proposals and applications, site inspections, preparing estimates, and completing tender-related procedures. The project has been targeted for completion by December 31, 2026.

national_raw_news.title: Ganeshotsav Concludes Across Country with Ganesh Idol Immersions on Anant Chaturdashi 2 hours ago 69
national_raw_news.content: The auspicious festival of Ganeshotsav is concluding today across the country, including Maharashtra, on the occasion of Anant Chaturdashi. The festival, which began on Ganesh Chaturthi, is culminating with the immersion of Ganesh idols as thousands of devotees turn out to bid farewell to their beloved deity. Immersion processions of prominent and prestigious public Ganeshotsav mandals have commenced in several major cities across the state. Civic authorities and police have made extensive arrangements to ensure the smooth and safe conduct of the processions. In Mumbai, grand Ganesh immersion processions have begun, with the city resonating with dhol-tasha beats and chants of “Ganpati Bappa Morya.” Large crowds have gathered across the city to accompany the idols to immersion sites. Processions of iconic idols, including Lalbaugcha Raja, Mumbaicha Raja at Ganesh Galli, Tejukaya, Chinchpokli’s Chintamani and Borivali’s Upnagracha Raja, have commenced amid music and large gatherings of devotees. The Maharashtra Tourism Department has set up a special viewing pavilion at Girgaon Chowpatty, where foreign tourists can witness the grand immersion ceremony and experience Mumbai’s vibrant cultural traditions. This year, arrangements have been made at 67 natural immersion sites, including Girgaon Chowpatty, Dadar and Juhu, along with more than 383 artificial ponds. Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde has appealed to citizens to opt for artificial ponds wherever possible to help protect the environment. Lifeguards and more than 24,000 police personnel have been deployed across the city. Drones are being used for surveillance at key locations, while noise levels are also being monitored to control noise pollution during the processions. In Pune, immersion processions for the city’s five Manache Ganpati, or most revered Ganesha idols, have begun. The first revered idol, Kasba Ganpati, set out for immersion at around 10 am. Traffic diversions have been introduced in central areas to facilitate the processions, while heavy police security has been deployed. In Nagpur, citizens have responded positively to the Municipal Corporation’s initiative to reduce pollution in rivers and lakes by opting to immerse idols in artificial ponds established across the city. In Nashik, the Ganesh immersion procession began in the presence of Guardian Minister Girish Mahajan. A total of 25 Ganesh mandals are participating in the procession. The Nashik Municipal Corporation has designated 77 official immersion sites and made special arrangements for collecting household Ganesh idols under its ‘Idol Donation’ initiative. In Khamgaon in Buldhana district, the immersion procession began at 9 am with the Maha-Aarti of the revered Wooden Ganpati, or Manacha Ganpati. Arrangements for Ganesh immersion have been made at several locations in Dhule, including the Panjara River. In Nandurbar, devotees are eagerly awaiting the traditional Harihar Bhet, or meeting of the deities, between the ‘Dada’ and ‘Baba’ Ganpati idols, scheduled to take place at midnight. Ganesh immersion festivities are also underway across Jalna district. The Municipal Corporation has arranged for immersion at the kund at Motitalav. The main immersion procession featuring the revered Manacha Ganpati is scheduled to pass through the city in the evening. In Nanded, Ganesh immersion is taking place to the accompaniment of traditional instruments, without DJs. The city’s idol collection centres are also receiving a good response. The Municipal Corporation has established 17 idol collection centres and 10 artificial immersion tanks at various locations. In Latur, the lack of rainfall this year has resulted in rivers, streams and other natural water sources drying up. With water unavailable for immersion, the eco-friendly Ganesh idol collection centres established by the Latur Municipal Corporation are receiving an enthusiastic response from devotees.
